newsitem.title: USA: Man accused of trying to defraud Christie's.
newsitem.headline: Man accused of trying to defraud Christie's.

text.p: An Illinois man was accused Wednesday of trying to defraud Christie's auction house in connection with the sale of a fabled emerald-encrusted crown.
The U.S. Attorney's office in Chicago said a grand jury indicted Richard Piper, 59, Scales Mound, Illinois, on charges of mail and wire fraud and attempted extortion.

The indictment alleged that Piper falsely told Christie's of New York that he had letters proving his late father owned a share of the Crown of the Andes, a bejeweled item from the Cathedral of Popayan that was valued at as much as $5 million.
Piper allegedly demanded a share of the sale price as Christie's prepared to auction the artifact a year ago and threatened to go to court to block the sale.
The auction proceeded despite Piper's claims but the crown, which has 447 Colombian emeralds and dates to the early 1600s, failed to sell.

Piper's late father was part of a syndicate that bought the crown to the United States in the 1930s where it attracted huge crowds at exhibits. The indictment alleged that Piper's father later defaulted on his share of the payments for the item and lost his claim to ownership.
